To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) proton-induced degradation of Chandra CCDs is dominated by the effects of ionizing events, (2) the degradation of charge transfer efficiency is caused by the creation of traps, and (3) the observed amount of on- orbit degradation can be accounted-for using a proton spectrum that has the same spectral shape as the spectrum that is incident on the spacecraft, but that has an intensity that is reduced by /spl sim/5 orders of magnitude.

the amount of on-or-bit proton-induced degradation of the Advanced CCD Imaging Spectorometer (ACIS) is less than the amount predicted by ground-based measurements and that the amount of degradation can be accounted by a proton spectrum at ACIS location that has the shape of the spectrum incident on Chandra but a reduced fluence.
the degradation of Chandra CCDs is dominated by the effects of protons with energies below 1 MeV.
